# Jewels that modify the tree

_Generated from PoB tree data `3.29`. Regenerate after any data update._

Three families rewrite the passive tree itself: cluster jewels grow new nodes, historic
jewels transform existing ones by seed, and a handful of radius/rule jewels transform,
re-grant or re-wire what is already there. Plain stat jewels are ordinary affix items -
`affixes.lua "Cobalt Jewel"` etc.

# Cluster jewels

Cluster jewels socket into the tree's outer rim and grow new passive nodes. The
subgraph PoB builds always matches the in-game structure.

## Mechanics, verified headless

- Only rim sockets take a Large jewel: `node.expansionJewel.size == 2`
  (`PassiveSpec.lua:1764`). Every rim socket costs ~2 travel + the socket itself.
- Subgraph nodes are real allocated nodes: they count toward the 122+extras passive
  budget (`CountAllocNodes`), and `validate.lua`'s tree check covers them.
- The jewel's skill, node count AND socket count come from its ENCHANT lines, parsed by
  exact text (`ModParser.lua:6544`, `:5199`). The `Cluster Jewel Skill:`/`Node Count:`
  properties are only crafting-UI state - without the enchant lines the subgraph never
  builds, and without the socket enchant line no socket nodes grow.
- Notables come from the generated "1 Added Passive Skill is X" lines, so an uncrafted
  jewel builds a subgraph of only small passives. Run `craft.lua`, as with every
  authored item.
- Notable legality = spawn weight with the jewel's skill tag passed as an include tag
  (`ItemsTab.lua:2150`); `affixes.lua --skill=<tag>` and `validate.lua` both do this.

## Nested sockets

Every Large carries "2 Added Passive Skills are Jewel Sockets", every Medium
"1 Added Passive Skill is a Jewel Socket", Smalls none - author these enchant lines,
they are part of the node count (smalls = count - sockets - notables). A nested socket
takes a smaller cluster jewel (Large holds Medium/Small, Medium holds Small) OR any
regular jewel, abyss jewels included - the one place a plain abyss jewel fits a tree
socket. Abyss HISTORICS are the reverse: their conquest data is keyed to base tree
sockets only, so nested placement does nothing (verified: zero conquered nodes).

This is the quiet half of cluster value: a nested socket is a 1-point jewel socket
where tree sockets cost 2-3. Nested socket nodes get STABLE tree ids (proxy nodes, not
generated ids) - craft, load, read the ids off the subgraph, then reference them in
`Spec/Sockets` like any socket. Verified round-trip: save and reload reproduce the
same ids, figures identical; `validate.lua` checks jewels in nested sockets like any
other slot.

## Authoring recipe (proven)

```
Rarity: RARE
Some Name
Large Cluster Jewel
Crafted: true
Item Level: 84
Cluster Jewel Skill: affliction_fire_damage
Cluster Jewel Node Count: 8
Prefix: {range:0.85}AfflictionNotablePrismaticHeart__
Prefix: {range:0.85}AfflictionNotableSmokingRemains
Implicits: 3
{enchant}Adds 8 Passive Skills
{enchant}2 Added Passive Skills are Jewel Sockets
{enchant}Added Small Passive Skills grant: 12% increased Fire Damage
```

The last enchant line must be the skill's exact enchant text - `skills.enchant` in
`jewels.db` (see Querying below).
Socket via `<Socket nodeId="..." itemId="..."/>` on a rim socket, allocate the socket
node, then the subgraph nodes (generated ids land in the saved `nodes` list and reload
cleanly). Craft first, then allocate - notables only exist after crafting.

## Stat-stick clusters

Notables are not the only design. The `AfflictionJewelSmallPassivesGrant*` prefixes add
a stat to EVERY small ("Added Small Passive Skills also grant: ..."), and
`AfflictionJewelSmallPassivesHaveIncreasedEffect2` multiplies all of it by 35%. A
12-passive Large with no notables and three "also grant" mods is 12 custom-designed
small passives - e.g. life + attributes + armour on every node. `affixes.lua
"<size> Cluster Jewel" --skill=<tag>` lists these alongside the notables.

## Point economics

A jewel is worth `socket path (~3) + smalls walked + notables taken` points. Compare
against the tree wheel it replaces: smalls only pay if the enchant stat is live (a
15%-crit small is dead at 100% crit), so count notables per point, not nodes per point,
and count nested sockets as saved points against the 2-3 a tree socket costs.

Measured on the 3.29 CoC Blazing Salvo build (7.03m baseline):

- Medium crit (Pressure Points + Eye of the Storm): 7 points, +351k = 50k/pt -
  crit capped, so all four 15%-crit smalls were dead.
- Large fire (Prismatic Heart + Smoking Remains), no sockets: 8 points, +831k =
  104k/pt - 12%-fire smalls live, on par with the tree's last picks (~120-290k/pt).
- Same Large with its 2 sockets holding a Medium crit cluster and an ES/fire abyss
  jewel: 13 points, +1.88m and +136 ES = 145k/pt - the nested sockets beat everything.

## Querying jewels.db

Cluster skills and notables live in `data/jewels.db`, rebuilt with this file. A
notable name from memory is a hypothesis - query it; zero rows means removed or
never existed, same verdict either way (removed notables keep spawn weight 0 in
PoB, so `affixes.lua` and `validate.lua` also reject them by weight).

- `sizes(name, min_nodes, max_nodes, sockets, socket_enchant)` - the socket
  enchant line each size must author.
- `skills(size, id, tag, small_stats, enchant)` - per size x skill; `enchant` is
  the exact final enchant line for authoring; `tag` is the weight key notables
  roll against and the `--skill=` argument to `affixes.lua`.
- `notables(id, name, mod_id)` - `mod_id` is the Prefix affix id to author.
- `notable_weights(notable_id, tag, weight)` - the skill tags that roll it;
  weight is relative within the tag's pool.
- `notable_stats(notable_id, ord, line, template)` - stat lines from the tree's
  own nodes; `template` has every number as `#` - LIKE-match on it, not `line`.
- `meta(key, value)` - `tree_version`, `generated_at`.

Canonical queries:

```sh
DB=.claude/skills/cook/data/jewels.db
# notables a fire cluster can roll, with stats and authoring ids
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT n.name, n.mod_id, s.line FROM notables n
  JOIN notable_weights w ON w.notable_id=n.id AND w.tag='affliction_fire_damage'
  LEFT JOIN notable_stats s ON s.notable_id=n.id ORDER BY n.name, s.ord;"
# criteria search across every notable, and which tags carry the hits
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT DISTINCT n.name, w.tag FROM notables n
  JOIN notable_stats s ON s.notable_id=n.id
  JOIN notable_weights w ON w.notable_id=n.id
  WHERE s.template LIKE '%Critical Strike Multiplier%';"
# a size's skills with their authoring enchant lines
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT id, small_stats, enchant FROM skills WHERE size='Medium Cluster Jewel';"
```
# Historic jewels

Seed-based node transformation. **The whole character gets ONE historic** - all eleven
carry `Limited to: 1 Historic`. PoB enforces it silently: the first-socketed jewel wins,
every later one gets `item.jewelData.limitDisabled = true` and contributes nothing.
Check that flag when a historic seems dead.

## The six radius timeless jewels

Socket in any tree socket; every node in Large radius is conquered. What happens then
(PassiveSpec.lua:1191+, verified headless):

- **Keystones** become the conqueror's keystone - fixed by VARIANT, the seed never
  matters. The keystone is the parenthesised name in the tables below.
- **Notables** roll on the seed: replaced by a legion notable or given legion additions.
  Sweep seeds by measuring; there is no shortcut reasoning.
- **Small passives** are deterministic per legion:

| legion | small passives | attribute smalls |
|---|---|---|
| Karui (Lethal Pride) | keep stats, +4 Strength | +2 Strength |
| Maraketh (Brutal Restraint) | keep stats, +4 Dexterity | +2 Dexterity |
| Kalguur (Heroic Tragedy) | keep stats, +2% increased Ward | +1% Ward |
| Templar (Militant Faith) | keep stats, +5 Devotion | replaced by +10 Devotion node |
| Eternal (Elegant Hubris) | REPLACED BY BLANK - stats wiped | blanked too |
| Vaal (Glorious Vanity) | rerolled from seed - anything | rerolled |

| jewel | legion | seed (item text) | conquerors -> keystone granted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brutal Restraint | Maraketh | 500-8000 | Asenath -> Dance with Death; Deshret -> Wind Dancer LEGACY, not obtainable; Nasima -> Second Sight; Balbala -> The Traitor |
| Elegant Hubris | Eternal Empire | 2000-160000 | Cadiro -> Supreme Decadence; Chitus -> Supreme Ego LEGACY, not obtainable; Victario -> Supreme Grandstanding; Caspiro -> Supreme Ostentation |
| Glorious Vanity | Vaal | 100-8000 | Doryani -> Corrupted Soul; Xibaqua -> Divine Flesh; Zerphi -> Eternal Youth LEGACY, not obtainable; Ahuana -> Immortal Ambition |
| Heroic Tragedy | Kalguur | 100-8000 | Vorana -> Black Scythe Training; Uhtred -> Celestial Mathematics; Medved -> The Unbreaking Circle |
| Lethal Pride | Karui | 10000-18000 | Kaom -> Strength of Blood; Kiloava -> Glancing Blows LEGACY, not obtainable; Rakiata -> Tempered by War; Akoya -> Chainbreaker |
| Militant Faith | Templars | 2000-10000 | Avarius -> Power of Purpose; Dominus -> Inner Conviction; Venarius -> The Agnostic LEGACY, not obtainable; Maxarius -> Transcendence |

Elegant Hubris item-text seeds run 2000-160000 in steps of 20; internally PoB divides by
20 (seed ranges validated against `data.timelessJewelSeedMin/Max`). Selecting a LEGACY
conqueror variant fails `validate.lua`'s unique check.

Militant Faith additionally has two selectable devotion mods (`Has Alt Variant` /
`Has Alt Variant Two` + `Selected Alt Variant:`/`Selected Alt Variant Two:`), chosen from:

- 4% increased Area Damage per 10 Devotion
- 3% increased Mana Cost Efficiency per 10 Devotion
- Channelling Skills deal 4% increased Damage per 10 Devotion
- 4% increased Elemental Damage per 10 Devotion
- +2% to all Elemental Resistances per 10 Devotion
- 1% reduced Mana Cost of Skills per 10 Devotion
- Regenerate 0.6 Mana per Second per 10 Devotion
- Minions have +60 to Accuracy Rating per 10 Devotion
- 1% increased Minion Attack and Cast Speed per 10 Devotion
- 1% increased effect of Non-Curse Auras per 10 Devotion
- 3% increased Effect of non-Damaging Ailments on Enemies per 10 Devotion
- 4% reduced Duration of Curses on you per 10 Devotion
- 4% reduced Elemental Ailment Duration on you per 10 Devotion
- 3% increased Defences from Equipped Shield per 10 Devotion
- 4% increased Brand Damage per 10 Devotion
- 4% increased Totem Damage per 10 Devotion

## The five abyss historics

Abyss jewel bases; their conquest data is keyed to **base tree sockets only** - in a
cluster jewel's nested socket they conquer nothing (verified), and they have no other
stats, so nested placement is fully dead. The conquered set is baked per (seed, socket)
in the LUT: nodes near the socket are wholesale REPLACED with new abyss identities
(smalls and notables both; verified 58 nodes from one socket). Zorath's jewel instead
conquers the nodes along your CURRENT shortest allocated path from its socket to the
class start - reallocate the tree and the conquest moves with it (verified, 6 nodes).

| jewel | base | lord | seed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baleful Dominion | Hypnotic Eye Jewel | Kurgal | 100-8000 |
| Destructive Aspiration | Ghastly Eye Jewel | Amanamu | 100-8000 |
| Extinguishing Grasp | Searching Eye Jewel | Ulaman | 100-8000 |
| Festering Vengeance | Murderous Eye Jewel | Tecrod | 100-8000 |
| Reclaimed Malevolence | Assembled Eye Jewel | Zorath | 100-8000 |

## Authoring and measuring historics headless

```
Rarity: UNIQUE
Lethal Pride
Timeless Jewel
Limited to: 1 Historic
Radius: Large
Implicits: 0
Commanded leadership over 12000 warriors under Kaom
Passives in radius are Conquered by the Karui
Historic
```

Write the seed line CONCRETE (validate checks it in range against the current variants).
Socket, refresh, then read `node.conqueredBy` / `node.sd` off the spec - conquests are
recomputed inside `BuildAllDependsAndPaths`, so they are always current. Seed hunting is
a sweep: loop seeds, edit the one number in the raw, re-parse, refresh, measure - or
call `data.readLUT(seed, nodeId, jewelType)` directly for a single node's outcomes
(types 1-6 in `data.timelessJewelTypes` order).

The LUTs ship as zlib streams (`src/Data/TimelessJewelData/*.zip*`, multi-part files
concatenated). HeadlessWrapper stubs `Inflate`/`Deflate` to return `""`; the kitchen's
`pob.lua` rebinds both through `runtime/zlib1.dll`, without which every notable reports
`Missing LUT` and abyss jewels CRASH the calc on socketing. First legion-jewel load also
rewrites the `.bin` caches the GUI uses; abyss data (~28 MB compressed each) is inflated
once per process and cached in memory only.

# Radius and rule-changing jewels

Obtainable uniques that transform, re-grant or re-wire existing nodes (plain "per X in
Radius" counters just READ the tree and are excluded). Multi-variant lines are shown as
the variant list.

## Radius auras - every allocated passive in radius also grants the stat

**The Light of Meaning** (Prismatic Jewel, radius Large, limit 1)
- one of: Passive Skills in Radius also grant +2 to all Attributes / Passive Skills in Radius also grant +4% to Chaos Resistance / Passive Skills in Radius also grant +5 to maximum Life / Passive Skills in Radius also grant +5 to maximum Mana / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 6% increased Chaos Damage / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 6% increased Cold Damage / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 5% increased Global Critical Strike Chance / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 7% increased Evasion Rating / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 6% increased Fire Damage / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 6% increased Lightning Damage / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 3% increased Energy Shield / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 6% increased Physical Damage / Passive Skills in Radius also grant 7% increased Armour

## Effect rewriters - nodes in radius grant more, less or nothing

**Might of the Meek** (Crimson Jewel, radius Large)
- 50% increased Effect of non-Keystone Passive Skills in Radius
- Notable Passive Skills in Radius grant nothing

**Unnatural Instinct** (Viridian Jewel, radius Small, limit 1)
- Allocated Small Passive Skills in Radius grant nothing
- Grants all bonuses of Unallocated Small Passive Skills in Radius

**Voices** (Large Cluster Jewel)
- Adds 3 Jewel Socket Passive Skills
- one of: Adds 1 Small Passive Skill which grants nothing / Adds 3 Small Passive Skills which grant nothing / Adds 5 Small Passive Skills which grant nothing / Adds 7 Small Passive Skills which grant nothing
